correctness.rationale: The displayed ensemble is exact and normalized. Each component is product across one cut, forcing its pure \(R_2\) to zero. The equal mixture is permutation symmetric; exact partial transposition gives a three-dimensional block with eigenvalues \(0,\pm\sqrt2/6\), so every one-qubit cut is NPT. For each fixed cut, the source seed \(\xi_\Gamma\) is continuous, nonnegative, and zero exactly on cut-product pure states. In finite dimension its convex roof attains its minimum; a zero minimum therefore exists exactly for cut-separable mixed states. Since the witness is entangled across all three cuts, all fixed-cut roofs and hence \(R_2\) are strictly positive. Sources: arXiv:0911.4245, Eqs. (10)--(15); exact bundled replay. Risk: none affecting the proof; no numerical lower bound on the positive \(R_2\) value is asserted.

value.rationale: The witness is mathematically motivated by the distinction between fixed-bipartition separability and the convex hull of states separable across varying cuts. It shows that a published mixed multipartite construction can be positive on an explicitly biseparable state even though each ensemble component has zero pure value, and identifies the order of convex-roofing and geometric aggregation as the mechanism. Later GME work uses the opposite order, underscoring the structural relevance. Sources: arXiv:0911.4245, arXiv:quant-ph/0602143, arXiv:2112.10509, and standard mixed-state GME definitions such as arXiv:2201.08694. Risk: the result is a sharp counterexample rather than a complete classification of all nonconvex mixtures.
